questions.question: Describe the structure of neuron.
questions.solution_html:
• Labelled diagram of neuron – (1 mark)
  •  Cell body - known as soma or perikaryon
  •  Constituted by a mass of cytoplasm called neuroplasm
  •  The cytoplasm contains a large nucleus, Nissl bodies, neurofibrils
  • mitochondria and Golgi apparatus.
  •  Nissl bodies and neurofibrils are found only in nerve cell and not in other
  • cells.
  •  Dendrons - branched process of neuron and it is branched repeatedly to
  • form dendrites.
  •  Dendrites transmits impulses towards the nerve cell body
  •  Axon - the longer process of nerve cell.
  •  Axon arises from axon hillock of the nerve cell body
  •  Axon transmits impulses away from the nerve cell body.
  •  Axon has a long central core of cytoplasm called axoplasm.
  •  Axoplasm is covered by the tubular sheath like membrane called axolemma.
  •  Axon is divided into small branches called axon endings or telodendrons
  • with bulb like structures at the end called synaptic knob or terminal buttons.
  •  Inside synaptic knobs, several secretory vesicles called synaptic vesicles are
  • present. They secrete and store neurotransmitters like acetylcholine.
  •  Axon is covered by a membrane called neurilemma. It is also called
  • neurilemmal sheath or sheath of Schwann. It contains Schwann cells.
  •  Some nerve fibres are covered by one more membrane called medullary or
  • myelin sheath. They are called medullated or myelinated nerve fibres.
  •  Myelin sheath is a thick lipoprotein sheath that insulates the myelinated
  • nerve fiber. It is absent at regular intervals.
  •  The area where myelin sheath is absent is called node of Ranvier. It acts as
  • an insulating jacket for axon. (1/(4 mark) for each point)
questions.final_answer: an insulating jacket for axon. (1/ for each point)

questions.question: Explain Astigmatism.
questions.solution_html:
• Astigmatism
  •  The condition in which light rays are not brought to a sharp point upon retina.
  • When it is moderate, it is known as physiological astigmatism. When it is well
  • marked, it is considered abnormal.
  •  In a normal eye, lens has approximately same curvature in all meridians. So, the
  • light rays are refracted almost equally in all meridians and brought to a focus.
  •  If the curvature is different in different meridians, vertical, horizontal and oblique
  • the refractive power is also different in different meridians.
  •  The meridian with greater curvature refracts the light rays more strongly than the
  • other meridians. So, these light rays are brought to a focus in front of the light rays
  • which pass through other meridians. Such irregularity of curvature of lens causes
  • astigmatism.
  •  Astigmatism is corrected by using cylindrical glass lens having the convexity in the
  • meridians, corresponding to that of lens of eye having a lesser curvature, i.e. if the
  • horizontal curvature of lens is less, the person should use cylindrical glass lens with
  • the convexity in horizontal meridian. ((1 mark) for each point)
questions.final_answer: the convexity in horizontal meridian. ( for each point)

questions.question: Explain synapse.
questions.solution_html:
• Synapse - The junction between two neurons is called synapse. It is through this
  • junction that an impulse pass from one neuron to other. ((1 Mark))
  •  Classification of Synapse - Anatomical classification and Functional
  • classification (1/(2 mark))
  • Anatomical Classification
  • a) Axoaxonic synapse in which axon of one neuron terminates on axon of another
  • neuron. (1/(2 mark))
  • b) Axodendritic synapse in which the axon of one neuron terminates on dendrite of
  • another neuron. (1/(2 mark))
  • c) Axosomatic synapse in which axon of one neuron ends on soma (cell body) of
  • another neuron. (1/(2 mark))
  • Functional classification
  • a) Electrical synapse
  •  Synapse in which the physiological continuity between the presynaptic and the
  • post synaptic neurons is provided by gap junction between the two neurons.
  •  Direct exchange of ions between the two neurons through the gap junction.
  •  The action potential reaching the terminal portion of presynaptic neuron
  • directly enters the postsynaptic neuron. Important feature of electrical synapse
  • is that the synaptic delay is very less because of the direct flow of current.
  •  This type of impulse transmission occurs in some tissues like the cardiac
  • muscle fibers, smooth muscle fibers of intestine and the epithelial cells of lens
  • in the eye. ((1 mark) – ¼ mark for each point)
  • b) Chemical synapse
  • - junction between a nerve fiber and a muscle fiber or between two nerve fibers
  • through which the signals are transmitted by the release of chemical transmitter.
  • - No continuity between the two neurons because of the presence of a space called
  • synaptic cleft between the two neurons.
  • - Action potential reaching the presynaptic terminal causes release of
  • neurotransmitter substance
  • - Neurotransmitter reaches the postsynaptic neuron through synaptic cleft and
  • causes the production of potential change. ((1 mark) – ¼ mark for each point)
questions.final_answer: Option Axoaxonic synapse in which axon of one neuron terminates on axon of another

questions.question: Describe the structure of neuron.
questions.solution_html:
• Labelled diagram of neuron – (1 mark)
  •  Cell body - known as soma or perikaryon
  •  Constituted by a mass of cytoplasm called neuroplasm
  •  The cytoplasm contains a large nucleus, Nissl bodies, neurofibrils
  • mitochondria and Golgi apparatus.
  •  Nissl bodies and neurofibrils are found only in nerve cell and not in other
  • cells.
  •  Dendrons - branched process of neuron and it is branched repeatedly to
  • form dendrites.
  •  Dendrites transmits impulses towards the nerve cell body
  •  Axon - the longer process of nerve cell.
  •  Axon arises from axon hillock of the nerve cell body
  •  Axon transmits impulses away from the nerve cell body.
  •  Axon has a long central core of cytoplasm called axoplasm.
  •  Axoplasm is covered by the tubular sheath like membrane called axolemma.
  •  Axon is divided into small branches called axon endings or telodendrons
  • with bulb like structures at the end called synaptic knob or terminal buttons.
  •  Inside synaptic knobs, several secretory vesicles called synaptic vesicles are
  • present. They secrete and store neurotransmitters like acetylcholine.
  •  Axon is covered by a membrane called neurilemma. It is also called
  • neurilemmal sheath or sheath of Schwann. It contains Schwann cells.
  •  Some nerve fibres are covered by one more membrane called medullary or
  • myelin sheath. They are called medullated or myelinated nerve fibres.
  •  Myelin sheath is a thick lipoprotein sheath that insulates the myelinated
  • nerve fiber. It is absent at regular intervals.
  •  The area where myelin sheath is absent is called node of Ranvier. It acts as
  • an insulating jacket for axon. (1/(4 mark) for each point)
questions.final_answer: an insulating jacket for axon. (1/ for each point)

questions.question: Explain Astigmatism.
questions.solution_html:
• Astigmatism
  •  The condition in which light rays are not brought to a sharp point upon retina.
  • When it is moderate, it is known as physiological astigmatism. When it is well
  • marked, it is considered abnormal.
  •  In a normal eye, lens has approximately same curvature in all meridians. So, the
  • light rays are refracted almost equally in all meridians and brought to a focus.
  •  If the curvature is different in different meridians, vertical, horizontal and oblique
  • the refractive power is also different in different meridians.
  •  The meridian with greater curvature refracts the light rays more strongly than the
  • other meridians. So, these light rays are brought to a focus in front of the light rays
  • which pass through other meridians. Such irregularity of curvature of lens causes
  • astigmatism.
  •  Astigmatism is corrected by using cylindrical glass lens having the convexity in the
  • meridians, corresponding to that of lens of eye having a lesser curvature, i.e. if the
  • horizontal curvature of lens is less, the person should use cylindrical glass lens with
  • the convexity in horizontal meridian. ((1 mark) for each point)
questions.final_answer: the convexity in horizontal meridian. ( for each point)

questions.question: Explain synapse.
questions.solution_html:
• Synapse - The junction between two neurons is called synapse. It is through this
  • junction that an impulse pass from one neuron to other. ((1 Mark))
  •  Classification of Synapse - Anatomical classification and Functional
  • classification (1/(2 mark))
  • Anatomical Classification
  • a) Axoaxonic synapse in which axon of one neuron terminates on axon of another
  • neuron. (1/(2 mark))
  • b) Axodendritic synapse in which the axon of one neuron terminates on dendrite of
  • another neuron. (1/(2 mark))
  • c) Axosomatic synapse in which axon of one neuron ends on soma (cell body) of
  • another neuron. (1/(2 mark))
  • Functional classification
  • a) Electrical synapse
  •  Synapse in which the physiological continuity between the presynaptic and the
  • post synaptic neurons is provided by gap junction between the two neurons.
  •  Direct exchange of ions between the two neurons through the gap junction.
  •  The action potential reaching the terminal portion of presynaptic neuron
  • directly enters the postsynaptic neuron. Important feature of electrical synapse
  • is that the synaptic delay is very less because of the direct flow of current.
  •  This type of impulse transmission occurs in some tissues like the cardiac
  • muscle fibers, smooth muscle fibers of intestine and the epithelial cells of lens
  • in the eye. ((1 mark) – ¼ mark for each point)
  • b) Chemical synapse
  • - junction between a nerve fiber and a muscle fiber or between two nerve fibers
  • through which the signals are transmitted by the release of chemical transmitter.
  • - No continuity between the two neurons because of the presence of a space called
  • synaptic cleft between the two neurons.
  • - Action potential reaching the presynaptic terminal causes release of
  • neurotransmitter substance
  • - Neurotransmitter reaches the postsynaptic neuron through synaptic cleft and
  • causes the production of potential change. ((1 mark) – ¼ mark for each point)
questions.final_answer: Option Axoaxonic synapse in which axon of one neuron terminates on axon of another

questions.question: Discuss the term Diabetes Mellitus
questions.solution_html:
• Deficiency of insulin results in an elevation of blood glucose level.Increased levels
  • of glucose in the blood results in its elimination in urine along with large amounts of
  • water.The excessive loss of water through urine creates unusual thirst and the
  • consequent increased intake of water.These abnormalities in glucose metabolism and
  • associated symptoms due to the deficiency of insulin are collectively called diabetes
  • mellitus.((2 marks))

  • scaly. ((1 mark) each for point 2 -9)

questions.question: Explain nervous system.
questions.solution_html:
• Nervous system controls all the activities of the body. It is quicker than other control
  • system in the body. Nervous system is divided into two parts
  • CENTRAL NERVOUS SYSTEM
  • Central nervous system (CNS) includes brain and spinal cord. It is formed by neurons
  • and supporting cells called neuroglia. Structures of brain and spinal cord are arranged
  • in two layers, namely gray matter and white matter. Gray matter is formed by nerve
  • cell bodies and the proximal parts of nerve fibers, arising from nerve cell body. White
  • matter is formed by remaining parts of nerve fibers. ((2 mark))
  • part. Brain is situated in the skull. It is continued as spinal cord in the vertebral canal
  • through the foramen magnum of the skull bone. ((1 mark))
  • Brain and spinal cord are surrounded by three layers of meninges called the outer dura
  • mater, middle arachnoid mater and inner pia mater. The space between arachnoid
  • mater and pia mater is known as subarachnoid space. This space is filled with a fluid
  • called cerebrospinal fluid. Brain and spinal cord are actually suspended in the
  • cerebrospinal fluid. ((1 mark))
